notes: Historical EBIT is modeled as (Income before income taxes + Interest expense - net) using Eaton’s consolidated statements of income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

D&A equals 'Depreciation and amortization' from the consolidated cash flow statement; capex equals 'Capital expenditures for property, plant and equipment'. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

NWC is computed as (Accounts receivable - net + Inventory + Prepaid expenses and other current assets) minus (Accounts payable + Accrued compensation + Other current liabilities), excluding cash/short-term investments from current assets and excluding short-term debt/current portion of long-term debt from current liabilities. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

Cash used in the valuation bridge includes 'Cash' + 'Short-term investments' from the balance sheet; if your pipeline uses only cash & cash equivalents, adjust cash downward by the short-term investments component. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

2026 capex intensity in the forecast is calibrated to Eaton’s stated expectation of approximately $1.1 billion of capital expenditures for property, plant and equipment in 2026. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

Tax rate uses the effective tax rate discussed for FY2025; WACC/terminal growth/terminal margins are modeling assumptions (not explicitly disclosed by Eaton), included for completeness of the DCF input package. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

NOL balance is set to null because the 10-K provides tax loss carryforward information in deferred tax/valuation allowance terms rather than a single net 'NOL balance' figure suitable for direct carryforward scheduling in this schema. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

catalysts: Sustained order/backlog momentum in Electrical and Aerospace, translating into results that track or beat 2026 guidance. ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))

Execution of the 2026 capex and capacity expansion plan; resulting operating leverage as investments translate into throughput and mix. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

Potential corporate actions referenced by management (e.g., Mobility separation progress and acquisition integration dynamics). ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))
company_overview: Eaton is an intelligent power management company serving data center, utility, industrial, commercial and institutional, machine building, residential, aerospace, and mobility markets. ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))

Business is organized around Electrical Americas, Electrical Global, and Aerospace (with Vehicle and eMobility as additional reporting segments). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))

FY2025 revenue was $27.4 billion, with record segment margins (24.5%) and strong cash generation (operating cash flow $4.5 billion). ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))

Company operates globally with customers across 180 countries. ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))
current_context: Q4 2025: record earnings per share and record segment margin (24.9%); backlog continued to grow, supported by order acceleration in Electrical Americas. ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))

FY2026 guidance (issued with Q4 2025 results): organic growth 7-9% and segment margins 24.6-25.0%. ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))

Company highlights disciplined capital planning supported by a growing and diversified backlog, improving confidence in predictable financial performance. ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))
Model setup reflects guidance (8% base organic growth for 2026) and partial margin normalization toward a ~0.195 EBIT margin terminal profile.
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue trajectory anchors on Eaton’s 2026 guidance and continued demand from data center and aerospace end-markets (with backlog and book-to-bill strength cited in the latest release). ([eaton.com](https://www.eaton.com/us/en-us/company/news-insights/news-releases/2026/eaton-reports-record-fourth-quarter-2025-results.html))
Margin outlook assumes gradual durability from current operating leverage rather than peak-cycle expansion; base EBIT margin tracks from ~0.19 toward ~0.195 by 2030.

Capex ramp supports capacity expansion: Eaton expects capital expenditures for property, plant and equipment of approximately $1.1 billion in 2026 (used to lift capex intensity in the forecast). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1551182/000155118226000007/etn-20251231.htm))
Working capital intensity is normalized from 2025 levels (higher NWC% observed historically) toward steadier levels as growth becomes more mature.
key_risks: Cyclicality and end-market weakness (notably industrial/vehicle/eMobility) could pressure sales growth and margin durability versus the modeled path.
Input cost volatility and supply chain disruptions could delay margin recovery or increase working capital needs.
Discount-rate/tax-rate uncertainty: model WACC and effective tax rate may differ from realized outcomes, affecting equity value sensitivity.

presentation.subtitle: Eaton (ETN) — DCF Valuation Input Package
valuation_summary: DCF base case uses gordon-growth terminal value (terminal growth 0.025) with conservative, economically consistent long-run assumptions relative to industrial fundamentals.

Peer comps are used as a sanity check for valuation ranges using EV/Revenue, EV/EBITDA, and forward P/E-type metrics (not a substitute for the DCF). ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/hon/statistics/))
Scenario analysis applies modest deltas to growth/margins and discount-rate/terminal-growth assumptions to reflect realistic uncertainty bands.
